system:
You are assembling a clinical visit note. The sentences of one note are listed below in random order with their section headings removed. File every sentence under one of these four headings: SUBJECTIVE, OBJECTIVE EXAM, OBJECTIVE RESULTS, ASSESSMENT AND PLAN. In the JSON, the headings are the keys subjective, objective_exam, objective_results and assessment_and_plan. Return each sentence ID under exactly one heading. Do not leave any sentence out and do not invent IDs.

SECTION DEFINITIONS
- SUBJECTIVE: what the patient reports and the history taken before the examination: the reason for the visit, the history of the present illness, the review of systems, past medical, surgical, family and social history, current medications and allergies.
- OBJECTIVE EXAM: what the clinician found on physical examination at this visit, including vital signs measured at the visit.
- OBJECTIVE RESULTS: results of laboratory tests, imaging and other studies that were reviewed.
- ASSESSMENT AND PLAN: the clinician's diagnoses or impressions, the reasoning behind them, treatment decisions, prescriptions, orders, referrals, patient instructions and follow-up.
A sentence goes under the heading that names its role in the note, not its topic. A symptom the patient reports belongs under SUBJECTIVE even if the plan discusses it again; a sentence that restates a symptom or finding to justify a decision belongs under ASSESSMENT AND PLAN.

For each sentence also give placement_confidence: HIGH, MEDIUM or LOW, meaning how sure you are that it belongs under that heading rather than another. If any sentence is LOW, set requires_review to true.

<sentences>
S1: His pain is localized to the lateral aspect of his left ankle and can be rated at 8 out of 10 without medication.
S2: Capillary refill is brisk at less than 3 seconds bilaterally.
S3: The onset of his pain began 2 days ago, when he stepped off of a curb and landed on his left ankle wrong.
S4: He will also be placed into an Aircast for ankle stabilization and will be provided crutches in order to remain non-weight-bearing.
S5: Musculoskeletal: Patient reports left ankle pain.
S6: I also advised him that his symptoms will likely start to improve significantly over the next 4 to 6 days.
S7: When taking ibuprofen his pain level is 7 out of 10.
S8: He states he has also iced and elevated his ankle.
S9: Tenderness to palpation laterally.
S10: He was able to ambulate back to his house after the incident but with pain.
S11: No joint laxity appreciated.
S12: NEURO: Normal strength and sensation bilaterally.
S13: Patient reports that he has been working from home since the start of COVID-19 and enjoys taking lots of walks.
S14: The nature of the diagnosis and treatment options were discussed.
S15: After reviewing the patient's examination and radiographic findings today, I have had a lengthy discussion with the patient in regards to his current symptoms.
S16: He denies any previous injuries to his left ankle.
S17: Matthew Murphy is a pleasant 20-year-old male who presents to the clinic today for the evaluation of left ankle pain.
S18: Strong dorsalis pedis pulses bilaterally.
S19: He will continue to take NSAIDs as needed for pain and swelling.
S20: At this time he will continue to follow the RICE protocol.
S21: Left ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex.
S22: No bony tenderness to palpation of the foot.
S23: Patient reports taking ibuprofen.
S24: We discussed that his symptoms are consistent with an ankle sprain of the lateral ligament complex.
S25: These reveal no fracture or bony abnormalities.
S26: The patient will follow up with me in 2 weeks to assess his progress, sooner if needed.
S27: We discussed that it may be a few days before he feels able to tolerate walking.
S28: He denies hearing a pop at the time of the injury, however, he describes his ankle as feeling extended and stretched.
